record.original_question: Fix p=c/n with c>0. Is it true that, with high probability for G_{n,p}, the width s(G_{n,p}) of the independence complex satisfies s(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1)) max_r |Q(G_{n,p})^(r)|?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9. Let p = cn−1, for some constant c > 0. Is it true with high probability that s(Gn,p) = (1 + o(1)) max r |Q(Gn,p) (r)|?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. Its independence complex I(G) is the simplicial complex whose faces are the independent sets of G. For a simplicial complex K, define its width s(K) to be the minimum, over orderings of the maximal faces (facets) F_1,F_2,...,F_m of K, of max_{1≤i≤m} |F_i \ (F_1 ∪ ... ∪ F_{i-1})|; write s(G):=s(I(G)).

For a graph G, let Q(G) denote the set of vertices of G that are not isolated, and for r≥0 let Q(G)^{(r)} be the set of vertices v ∈ Q(G) of degree exactly r in G (so |Q(G)^{(r)}| counts vertices of degree r that are not isolated). 

Let G_{n,p} denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph on n labelled vertices in which each edge appears independently with probability p, and fix p = c/n for a constant c > 0.

Question: Is it true that, with probability tending to 1 as n → ∞,
   s(G_{n,p}) = (1+o(1)) · max_{r ≥ 0} |Q(G_{n,p})^{(r)}| ?
